A preprocessing technique that decomposes the domain of viewing directions into 24 regions on a directional cube to extract a lower number of potentially visible voxels compared to the standard 6-region decomposition, improving extraction rate and rendering speed [S1, unofficial].

The claim is fully supported by the evidence in Source [S1]. The source explicitly states that decomposing the viewing direction domain into 24 regions (compared to 6) results in a lower percentage of extracted voxels (1.8% vs 3.4% for low resolution, and 0.9% vs 1.8% for high resolution). It further states that this modification 'significantly improves the extraction rate, making the rendering process much faster,' which aligns with the claim's assertion of improved extraction rate and rendering speed.
